Sources: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/parity.ts` - comparison, solid, and
Y-flip predicates.

### Diagnose

```ts
type ParitySuccessOrMismatch = {
  effect_id: string
  status: "ok" | "mismatch"
  maxDiff: number
  meanDiff: number
  mismatchCount: number
  mismatchPercent: number
  resolution: [number, number]
  glslSolid: boolean
  wgslSolid: boolean
  glslVariance: [number, number, number]
  wgslVariance: [number, number, number]
  yFlipDetected: boolean
  yFlipCleanFlip: boolean
  yFlipMismatchPercent: number
  yFlipMeanDiff: number
  yFlipRatio: number
  issues: string[]
  details: string
  console_errors?: string[]
}

type ParityFailure = {
  effect_id?: string
  status: "error"
  maxDiff?: 0
  meanDiff?: 0
  mismatchCount?: 0
  mismatchPercent?: 0
  resolution?: [number, number]
  details?: string
  error?: string
  console_errors?: string[]
}
```

Enumerated in-tool error details are `Failed to capture WebGL2`, `Failed to
capture WebGPU`, and
`Capture size mismatch: glsl <w>x<h> vs wgsl <w>x<h>`. Compile/browser failures
can instead use the outer `{effect_id,status:"error",error}` shape.

Issues include `GLSL SOLID COLOR (mean=...)`, `WGSL SOLID COLOR (mean=...)`, and
`Y-FLIP`/`PARTIAL Y-FLIP DETECTED (...)`. Solid-color and Y-flip issues do not
change `status`; status depends only on mismatch percentage. A strict gate must
also assert both solid flags false and `yFlipDetected === false` unless the
effect is intentionally solid.

There is no returned stale-selection, backend-switch, or identity-mismatch
failure shape. A parity result can name the requested `effect_id` while its
pixel buffers came from a previously ready graph or the same residual backend.
Diagnose that result as indeterminate outside the returned contract; the
missing machine-readable signal is GAP-024.

Backend compilation failures:

```ts
// Shared pipeline
{ code: "ERR_PROGRAM_SPEC_MISSING", program: string, pass: string }

// WebGL2
Error("Shader source missing for program '<id>'. You may need to regenerate the shader manifest.")
{ code: "ERR_SHADER_COMPILE", detail: string, source: string }
{ code: "ERR_SHADER_LINK", detail: string, program: string }
{ code: "ERR_UNIFORM_BLOCK_TOO_LARGE", detail: string, program: WebGLProgram }
{ code: "ERR_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND", pass: string, program: string }
{ code: "ERR_TOO_MANY_TEXTURES", pass: string, limit: number }

// WebGPU
{ code: "ERR_NO_WGSL_SOURCE", detail: string, program: string }
{ code: "ERR_SHADER_COMPILE", detail: string, program: string }
{ code: "ERR_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND", pass: string, program: string }
{ code: "ERR_TEXTURE_NOT_FOUND", pass: string, texture: string }
{ code: "ERR_NO_MRT_OUTPUTS", pass: string }
{ code: "ERR_COMPUTE_DISPATCH_UNRESOLVED", pass: string, detail: string }
```

Sources: backend compile/execute methods; Shade MCP
`src/tools/browser/parity.ts`.

<!-- SURFACE:MCP -->
## Shade MCP tool contracts

### Introspect

Use MCP `initialize`, send `notifications/initialized`, then call `tools/list`.
For the snapshot at the top of this document, `tools/list` returned the 18 verb
names documented below. Every tool descriptor declares
`inputSchema.$schema:"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"` and
`execution:{taskSupport:"forbidden"}`. None declares an `outputSchema`.
`renderEffectFrame.uniforms` and `runDslProgram.uniforms` are object schemas
with string `propertyNames` and numeric `additionalProperties`; the Zod 4
upgrade did not change their `Record<string,number>` application contract.

The transport result for every verb is:

```ts
type McpTextResult = {
  content: Array<{ type: "text", text: string /* JSON payload or plain error */ }>
  isError?: true
}
```

For normal handler returns, decode
`JSON.parse(result.content.find(x => x.type === "text").text)` before applying
the payload types below. Whole-call failures can instead carry plain error text
with `isError:true`; do not JSON-parse that path blindly. These tools do not
declare MCP structured content/output schemas; normal payload JSON is carried
as text.

The repository config supplies:

```text
SHADE_EFFECTS_DIR=./shaders/effects
SHADE_VIEWER_ROOT=.
SHADE_VIEWER_PATH=/demo/shaders/
SHADE_GLOBALS_PREFIX=__noisemaker
```

The package requires Node 22 or newer. Browser sessions are headless unless
`SHADE_HEADLESS` is `0` or `false`; `SHADE_SWIFTSHADER=1` or `true` opts into
Chromium's software rasterizer. `SHADE_TIMEOUT_MS` supplies the session default
for Playwright operations that honor it and is also used explicitly by backend,
status, and graph readiness polls. The parity six-frame warmup instead retains
an explicit `30000` ms bound.
`SHADE_AI_TIMEOUT_MS` bounds AI provider requests. Both configurable timeouts
are parsed with `parseInt(value, 10)` and default to `120000` ms when that result
is non-finite or nonpositive. Fractional text is truncated and a numeric prefix
followed by nonnumeric text is accepted.
`SHADE_AI_MODEL` overrides the provider model. Without an override, Anthropic
uses `claude-opus-5` and OpenAI uses `gpt-5.2`. SIGINT and SIGTERM close live
browser sessions and the shared viewer server before process exit.

The browser harness binds its temporary HTTP server to `127.0.0.1`. Viewer and
effect requests are confined to their configured roots after both lexical and
realpath checks; dotfiles, dot-directories, traversal, and symlink escapes are
rejected. Responses no longer add wildcard CORS. Known asset extensions receive
explicit media types and unlisted extensions remain serveable as
`application/octet-stream`. Successful file responses set `Vary: Origin` and
echo `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` only for an opaque `Origin: null` or an
`http`/`https` loopback origin on `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, or `localhost`, with an
optional port. Other origins receive no allow-origin header.

Sources: `.mcp.json`; `.codex/config.toml`; Shade MCP `package.json`;
`src/index.ts` - registration and shutdown; `src/config.ts`;
`src/ai/provider.ts`; `src/harness/browser-session.ts`;
`src/harness/live-sessions.ts`; `src/harness/server-manager.ts`;
`src/tools/browser/parity.ts` - warmup timeout.

### Act

Shared input and batch behavior:

```ts
type EffectSelector = {
  effect_id?: string
  effects?: string // comma-separated IDs; takes precedence over effect_id
}

type BrowserSelector = EffectSelector & {
  backend?: "webgl2" | "webgpu" // defaults to webgl2 where present
}

type Batched<T> = T | T[] // object for exactly one selected ID, array otherwise
type OuterEffectError = { effect_id: string, status: "error", error: string }
```

`effects` is split on commas and trimmed. Despite some tool descriptions, it is
not glob-expanded. With neither selector, `resolveEffectIds()` scans
`SHADE_EFFECTS_DIR`: one discovered effect is selected, multiple effects cause
an error, and a flat effect directory uses its basename. Filesystem analysis
tools reject absolute effect IDs and IDs containing `.` or `..` path segments
with `Invalid effect id: <id>` before reading. Browser selectors remain literal.
See GAP-018.

No numeric schema below uses Zod `.int()`, `.finite()`, `.min()`, `.max()`, or a
positive-resolution refinement unless explicitly stated. Descriptive ranges
are not validation.

Browser verbs call `BrowserSession.setBackend()` before capture/compile work.
That helper polls the page's current backend but exits silently when its timeout
expires, so the call is an attempt, not a verified switch. `compileEffect` and
`benchmarkEffectFPS` report the session's configured/requested backend string;
`renderEffectFrame` reports `pipeline.backend.getName()`; other browser results
often omit backend identity. Independently confirm the page backend before
accepting any requested-backend claim. See GAP-024.

#### compileEffect

```ts
type CompileEffectInput = EffectSelector & {
  backend?: "webgl2" | "webgpu" // default webgl2
}

type CompileEffectResult = Batched<
  | { effect_id: string, status: "ok" | "error", backend: string,
      passes: Array<{ id: string, status: "ok" | "error",
                      errors?: string[] }>,
      message: string, console_errors?: string[] }
  | OuterEffectError
>
```

The tool selects the effect and polls status text for up to the configured
`SHADE_TIMEOUT_MS` (default `120000` ms). On success it projects expanded passes
to `{id:p.name || "pass_<index>",status}`;
expanded passes normally have no `name`, so `pass_<index>` is expected. Success
message is `Compiled successfully`; timeout message is `Compile timeout`.

The status text can still describe the previous effect immediately after the
selection event. Its returned passes can therefore belong to the previous
graph while status is `ok`. Do not accept the pass list unless an independent
current-effect/graph identity check agrees. `testPixelParity` waits for a
noncompiling nonempty graph but has the same missing identity guarantee. This
is GAP-024.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/compile.ts` - `compileEffectSchema`,
`compileEffect()`.

#### renderEffectFrame

```ts
type RenderEffectFrameInput = BrowserSelector & {
  warmup_frames?: number                 // default 10
  capture_image?: boolean                // default false
  uniforms?: Record<string, number>
  time?: number                          // seconds; current deadlock risk
  resolution?: [number, number]
}

type RenderEffectFrameResult = Batched<RenderSuccess | RenderFailure>
```

Metric definitions, ranges, and thresholds are in Rendered output. A captured
image is a `data:image/png;base64,...` URI; otherwise `image_uri` is null.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/render.ts` -
`renderEffectFrameSchema`, `renderEffectFrame()`.

#### describeEffectFrame

```ts
type DescribeEffectFrameInput = EffectSelector & {
  prompt: string
  backend?: "webgl2" | "webgpu" // default webgl2
  capture_image?: boolean         // default false
}

type DescribeEffectFrameResult = Batched<
  | { effect_id: string, status: "ok",
      frame?: { image_uri: string },
      vision: Record<string, JsonValue> | null }
  | { effect_id: string, status: "error", error: string }
>
```

The intended AI JSON is `{description,tags,notes}`, but a parsed object is not
schema-checked. A parsed primitive or array and invalid JSON instead produce
`{description:<text>,tags:[],notes:null}`. `frame` is omitted unless
`capture_image` is true, avoiding an unsolicited base64 payload. Failure strings
include the common no-key message, `Failed to render frame`, and
`Failed to render frame: <render error>`.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/describe.ts` - schema and
`describeEffectFrame()`; `src/ai/provider.ts` - provider/no-key behavior.

#### benchmarkEffectFPS

```ts
type BenchmarkEffectFPSInput = BrowserSelector & {
  target_fps?: number       // default 60
  duration_seconds?: number // default 5
  resolution?: [number, number]
}

type BenchmarkEffectFPSResult = Batched<
  | { effect_id: string, status: "ok", backend: string,
      achieved_fps: number,
      meets_target: boolean,
      stats: {
        frame_count: number,
        avg_frame_time_ms: number,
        jitter_ms: number,
        min_frame_time_ms: number,
        max_frame_time_ms: number
      }, console_errors?: string[] }
  | OuterEffectError
>
```

`achieved_fps = frame_count/(sum(frame_times_ms)/1000)` and
`meets_target = achieved_fps >= target_fps`; the literal contract marker is
`fps >= target_fps`. Jitter is sample standard deviation with divisor
`frame_count-1`, or zero for at most one frame. Reported values are rounded to
two decimals. Tool status remains `ok` when `meets_target` is false; callers
must inspect the boolean. The tool now attempts `setBackend()` before selecting
the effect and measuring frames, but its returned `backend` is the configured
session/request value, not page-confirmed identity. See GAP-024.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/benchmark.ts` - schema and
`benchmarkEffectFPS()`.

#### testUniformResponsiveness

```ts
type TestUniformResponsivenessInput = BrowserSelector
type TestUniformResponsivenessResult = Batched<
  | ({ effect_id: string } & UniformResponsiveness)
  | OuterEffectError
>
```

The test set, perturbation rule, `luma_delta > 0.002` and
`max_channel_delta > 0.002` thresholds, and overall-status weakness are in
Parameters and globals. The tool switches to the requested backend before
selection, but the switch is not confirmed and capture still requires
`pipeline.backend.gl`. A WebGPU request returns the in-page baseline failure if
the switch succeeds, but can test residual WebGL output if the switch silently
times out. See GAP-024.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/uniforms.ts` - schema and
`testUniformResponsiveness()`.

#### testNoPassthrough

```ts
type TestNoPassthroughInput = BrowserSelector

type TestNoPassthroughResult = Batched<
  | { effect_id: string, status: "ok" | "passthrough",
      isFilterEffect: true,
      temporalDiff: number,       // normalized [0,1]
      uniqueColors: number,
      details: "Effect modifies input" |
               "Effect may be passing through unchanged",
      console_errors?: string[] }
  | { effect_id: string, status: "skipped" | "error",
      isFilterEffect: false, similarity: null, details: string,
      console_errors?: string[] }
  | OuterEffectError
>
```

The tool classifies an effect as a filter only when an expanded pass input value
contains the substring `input`. It captures WebGL frames at render times 0 and
1, samples with the same approximately-1000-pixel stride, and computes average
absolute RGB channel difference divided by 255. It returns `ok` when
`temporalDiff > 0.01` OR `uniqueColors > 5`. These are the literal returned
metric names. Nonfilters return `Not a filter effect`.
In-page failures include `No effect loaded` and `No GL context`.

The tool attempts to switch to the requested backend before selection. Because
its pixel capture requires `pipeline.backend.gl`, a confirmed WebGPU switch
returns `No GL context`; a silently failed switch can instead test residual
WebGL output. See GAP-024.

This test does not compare output to input; it compares output at two times and
color cardinality. A static varied passthrough can pass. See GAP-019.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/passthrough.ts` - schema and
`testNoPassthrough()`.

#### testPixelParity

```ts
type TestPixelParityInput = EffectSelector & {
  epsilon?: number // default 1, described 0..255 but not range-checked
  seed?: number    // default 42
}

type TestPixelParityResult = Batched<
  ParitySuccessOrMismatch | ParityFailure | OuterEffectError
>
```

All output fields and predicates are in Cross-backend parity.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/parity.ts` - schema and
`testPixelParity()`.

#### runDslProgram

```ts
type RunDslProgramInput = {
  dsl: string
  backend?: "webgl2" | "webgpu" // default webgl2
  warmup_frames?: number         // default 10
  capture_image?: boolean        // default false
  uniforms?: Record<string, number>
}

type RunDslProgramResult =
  | { status: "ok", backend: string,
      frame: { width: number, height: number, image_uri: string | null },
      metrics: {
        mean_rgb: Vec3,
        unique_sampled_colors: number,
        is_all_zero: boolean,
        is_monochrome: boolean
      }, console_errors?: string[] }
  | { status: "error", error: string, console_errors?: string[] }
```

Compilation attempts the page editor/run button, then renderer `compile()`, and
polls for up to the configured `SHADE_TIMEOUT_MS` (default `120000` ms).
Enumerated messages are `No DSL editor or renderer
found`, `Compile timeout`, `No renderer`, and `No GL context`, plus page status
or thrown compiler text. It directly requires `pipeline.backend.gl`, so a
WebGPU request cannot reach success. It does not return alpha, standard
deviation, luma variance, transparency, or low-luma-variance metrics.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/browser/dsl.ts` - schema and `runDslProgram()`.

#### checkEffectStructure

```ts
type CheckEffectStructureInput = { effect_id: string }

type CheckEffectStructureResult =
  | { status: "ok" | "warning",
      unusedFiles: string[],
      namingIssues: Array<{ type: "func" | "global", name: string,
                            reason: "Must be camelCase" }>,
      nameCollisions: Array<{
        type: "uniform_function" | "reserved_word" | "builtin_shadow",
        name: string, file: string, message: string
      }>,
      leakedInternalUniforms: string[],
      missingDescription: boolean,
      structuralParityIssues: Array<{
        type: "missing_wgsl" | "missing_glsl", program: string, message: string
      }>,
      requiredUniformIssues: unknown[],
      multiPass: boolean,
      passCount: number }
  | { status: "error", error: string }
```

Status is warning when any unused file, naming issue, name collision, leaked
internal uniform, missing description, or structural parity issue exists.
`requiredUniformIssues` is initialized but never populated or included in the
status predicate. Pass `name` values are not checked. GLSL reserved/builtin
collision checks use regex-extracted declarations.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/analysis/structure.ts` -
`checkEffectStructure()`.

#### checkAlgEquiv

```ts
type CheckAlgEquivInput = { effect_id: string }

type CheckAlgEquivResult =
  | { status: "ok" | "divergent",
      pairs: Array<{
        program: string,
        parity: "equivalent" | "divergent" | "error" | string,
        confidence?: "high" | "medium" | "low" | string,
        notes?: string,
        concerns?: string[],
        [key: string]: unknown
      }>,
      unmatchedGlsl?: string[],
      unmatchedWgsl?: string[],
      summary: string }
  | { status: "error", error: string }
```

Only same-stem `.glsl` and `.wgsl` files are paired; split `.vert`/`.frag` files
are ignored. AI JSON is not schema-validated. Overall divergence counts only
entries whose `parity` is exactly `divergent`; AI parse/error entries can leave
overall status `ok`. The returned `program` is written after the parsed AI
object, so it always remains the same-stem program matched from disk even if
the model emits its own value. Errors include the no-key message, `Missing glsl/
or wgsl/ directory`, and `No matching GLSL/WGSL pairs found`.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/analysis/alg-equiv.ts` - `checkAlgEquiv()`.

#### compareShaders

```ts
type CompareShadersInput = { effect_id: string }

type ShaderStructure = {
  lines: number
  functions: string[]
  uniforms: string[]
}

type CompareShadersResult = {
  status: "ok"
  programs: Array<
    | { program: string, glsl: ShaderStructure, wgsl: ShaderStructure,
        lineDiff: number, functionCountDiff: number }
    | { program: string, glsl: ShaderStructure | null,
        wgsl: ShaderStructure | null,
        note: "No WGSL counterpart" | "No GLSL counterpart" }
  >
  summary: string
}
```

Only `.glsl` and `.wgsl` files are scanned. Function/uniform detection uses
regex after comment stripping. This tool always returns status `ok`, including
missing counterparts; inspect `note` and null sides.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/analysis/compare.ts` - extractors and
`compareShaders()`.

#### analyzeBranching

```ts
type AnalyzeBranchingInput = {
  effect_id: string
  backend?: "webgl2" | "webgpu" // default webgl2
}

type AnalyzeBranchingResult =
  | ({ status: "ok" | "warning" } & Record<string, JsonValue>)
  | { status: "error", error: string }
```

GLSL mode reads `.glsl`; WebGPU reads `.wgsl`. AI output is not schema-
validated. The handler first computes `warning` when the sum of all returned
opportunity-array lengths is at least two and `ok` otherwise, irrespective of
severity. Parsed AI JSON is spread first and the computed `status` is written
last, so a model-provided field cannot overwrite the verdict. Callers must still
validate the untyped `shaders`, `opportunities`, and summary content before
using it. Errors before the AI call use `status:"error"` and include no AI key,
missing shader directory, and no shader files.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/analysis/branching.ts` -
`analyzeBranching()`.

#### searchEffects

```ts
type SearchEffectsInput = { query: string, limit?: number /* default 10 */ }
type SearchEffectsResult = {
  query: string
  results: Array<{ id: string, description: string,
                   tags: string[], score: number }>
  total: number
}
```

The query is lowercased, synonym-expanded, and whitespace-tokenized. Score is
an unbounded additive relevance number: full ID substring +20; per keyword ID
+8, name +15, description +5, tag +8, namespace +12. Only positive scores are
returned, descending, sliced to `limit`. The shared effect index is rebuilt
after five seconds; concurrent readers share one rebuild. An unparseable effect
is skipped with a server warning rather than represented in results. A rebuild
already in flight can survive explicit invalidation; see GAP-029.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/knowledge/search-effects.ts`;
`src/knowledge/effect-index.ts` - initialization and `search()`;
`src/knowledge/shared-instances.ts` - cache lifetime and rebuild sharing.

#### analyzeEffect

```ts
type AnalyzeEffectInput = { effect_id: string }
type AnalyzeEffectResult =
  | { effectId: string, name?: string, description?: string,
      namespace?: string, tags: string[],
      globals: Record<string, unknown>, passes: Array<Record<string, unknown>>,
      format: "js" | "json",
      shaders: Record<`glsl/${string}.glsl` | `wgsl/${string}.wgsl`, string> }
  | { error: string }
```

For `definition.js`, Shade uses a regex/balanced-brace projection rather than
importing the live class. It extracts only globals that contain a `uniform`, a
limited set of scalar fields, and pass `program` names; it does not reproduce
the full Noisemaker definition. Shader reads ignore split `.vert`/`.frag` files.
Use this tool for discovery, not full definition introspection. See GAP-017.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/knowledge/analyze-effect.ts`;
`src/formats/definition-js.ts` - `parseDefinitionJs()`.

#### searchShaderSource

```ts
type SearchShaderSourceInput = {
  query: string
  context_lines?: number // default 5
  limit?: number         // default 10
}
type SearchShaderSourceResult = {
  query: string
  matchCount: number
  results: Array<{
    effectId: string, file: string, lineNumber: number,
    matchLine: string, context: string
  }>
}
```

Only `.glsl` files are indexed. `query` is compiled case-insensitively as a
regular expression; invalid regex syntax is escaped and treated literally.
Context line numbers are one-based. After a match, nearby lines equal to the
context window are skipped.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/knowledge/search-source.ts`;
`src/knowledge/glsl-index.ts` - `search()`.

#### searchShaderKnowledge

```ts
type SearchShaderKnowledgeInput = {
  query: string
  category?: string
  limit?: number // default 5
}
type SearchShaderKnowledgeResult = {
  query: string
  category: string
  matchCount: number
  databaseStats: {
    totalDocuments: number, totalTerms: number, indexed: boolean,
    categories: Record<string, number>
  }
  results: Array<{
    title: string, category: string, score: number,
    snippet: string, tags?: string[], content?: string
  }>
}
```

Search uses synonym expansion and TF-IDF cosine similarity. Returned score is
rounded to three decimals and must be at least `0.05`; cosine similarity is in
`[0,1]`. Full `content` is included only for the first three results.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/knowledge/search-knowledge.ts`;
`src/knowledge/vector-db.ts` - `search()`, `getStats()`.

#### listEffects

```ts
type ListEffectsInput = { namespace?: string }
type ListEffectsResult = {
  namespace: string
  count: number
  effects: Array<{
    id: string, name: string | undefined, description: string,
    tags: string[], passes: number
  }>
}
```

Without a filter, `namespace` in output is `all`. The list uses Shade's lossy
definition projection; pass counts and names reflect that parser, not imported
Noisemaker class instances. It shares the five-second refreshable effect index
with `searchEffects` and its read-after-write caveat under GAP-029.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/utility/list-effects.ts`;
`src/knowledge/effect-index.ts` - `list()`;
`src/knowledge/shared-instances.ts` - shared refreshable index.

#### generateManifest

```ts
type GenerateManifestInput = Record<string, unknown> // schema has no properties and no additionalProperties:false; handler ignores args
type GenerateManifestResult =
  | { status: "ok", path: string, effectCount: number }
  | { error: string }
```

This verb writes `<SHADE_EFFECTS_DIR>/manifest.json` immediately with compact,
sorted JSON. It scans definition source with regexes for description, external
texture/mesh, tags, surface globals, and starter heuristics, and scans shader
files. A successful write clears the cached effect index. When no rebuild is
already in flight, the next list or search rescans immediately. An in-flight
rebuild remains shared and can repopulate the cache from a pre-write scan for
another five-second TTL; see GAP-029. It is state-changing; do not call during
read-only introspection. The only explicit error is
`Effects directory not found: <path>`; filesystem write exceptions escape the
handler.

Source: Shade MCP `src/tools/utility/generate-manifest.ts` -
`registerGenerateManifest()`; `src/knowledge/shared-instances.ts` - invalidation.

### Validate

A tool exchange is protocol-valid when it returns an MCP result rather than a
JSON-RPC/MCP `error`. That is not tool or domain success. Treat
`result.isError === true` as a tool-call failure first; its text can be plain
error text. Otherwise parse the JSON text and apply the verb-specific predicate:

| Verb | Domain pass predicate |
|---|---|
| `compileEffect` | every result `status === "ok"` and every pass status `ok` |
| `renderEffectFrame` | status `ok`, then output metrics/harness exemptions |
| `describeEffectFrame` | status `ok` and required application-specific vision fields present |
| `benchmarkEffectFPS` | status `ok` and `meets_target === true` |
| `testUniformResponsiveness` | status `ok` and every entry ends `:pass` |
| `testNoPassthrough` | `ok`, or `skipped` only for a confirmed nonfilter |
| `testPixelParity` | status `ok`, no disallowed solid/Y-flip flags |
| `runDslProgram` | status `ok`, then its limited metrics pass |
| `checkEffectStructure` | status `ok` and all issue arrays empty |
| `checkAlgEquiv` | status `ok`, every pair exactly `equivalent`, no unmatched lists |
| `compareShaders` | both sides non-null and no `note` for every program |
| `analyzeBranching` | validate the AI-derived fields; returned status is tool-computed as `warning` when opportunity count is `>=2`, `ok` otherwise |
| search/list/analyze | requested record present; these have no success status |
| `generateManifest` | status `ok`, then independently inspect the written diff |

Batch callers must validate every array member. Never treat transport success,
outer `status:"ok"`, or a nonempty result as universal validation.
For every browser verb, including `testPixelParity`, the listed predicate is
only meaningful after independent selected-effect, graph, and actual-backend
identity checks. The current returned payloads do not provide all three. See
GAP-024.

### Diagnose

Selector/scan failures thrown before per-effect loops include:

```text
Effects directory not found: <dir>. Specify effect_id or set SHADE_EFFECTS_DIR.
Failed to scan effects directory: <dir>
No effects found in <dir>. Specify effect_id.
Multiple effects found (<n>). Please specify effect_id or effects parameter. Available: ...
```

Browser tools usually catch per-effect exceptions as `OuterEffectError`.
Analysis/knowledge tools still use several incompatible payload forms:
`{status:"error",error}`, `{error}`, or unconditional `status:"ok"` plus notes.
The shared `toolResult()` wrapper marks a non-array top-level payload whose
status is `error` or whose `error` is a string with MCP `isError:true`; SDK-
caught thrown handler errors are also marked and may carry plain text. It does
not normalize the JSON payload, mark partial failures inside batch arrays, or
normalize verb-specific failures. All 18 ordinary handler return paths now use
the wrapper, but there is still no shared machine-readable domain failure
union. See GAP-020.

AI-dependent tools use this exact no-key message:

```text
No AI API key found. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, or create .anthropic/.openai file in project root.
```

Provider calls allow at most one retry. `describeEffectFrame` and
`checkAlgEquiv` request at most 1500 output tokens; `analyzeBranching` requests
at most 3000. Provider calls are bounded by `SHADE_AI_TIMEOUT_MS` as described
under Introspect.

Browser results can append `console_errors:string[]` through
`runWithConsoleCapture`, but field presence depends on the wrapper/result and
the messages are not categorized. Tool-specific failures are enumerated under
each verb above.

For `compileEffect`, `renderEffectFrame`, `describeEffectFrame`,
`benchmarkEffectFPS`, `testUniformResponsiveness`, `testNoPassthrough`,
`testPixelParity`, and `runDslProgram`, a domain-shaped `ok` response can still
be stale. Six wait on status text directly; `describeEffectFrame` delegates to
`renderEffectFrame`. `testPixelParity` instead waits for a noncompiling
nonempty graph, but effect selection only dispatches an asynchronous UI event,
and the wait does not bind the graph to the requested effect. No returned field
identifies that failure. `setBackend()` also returns without error if its
current-backend poll expires, and several results label only the requested
session backend or omit backend identity. Graph/effect/backend identity
disagreement must therefore be diagnosed outside the returned contract. This
is GAP-024.

Sources: Shade MCP `src/tools/resolve-effects.ts`; all tool registration files;
`src/ai/provider.ts` - `NO_AI_KEY_MESSAGE`;
`src/harness/browser-session.ts` - console capture.

## Fully worked, source-complete effect and validation finding

This instance is the repository's `synth/testPattern` effect. The three source
blocks below are complete, not excerpts. The MCP evidence was captured against
Noisemaker commit `f6b22ab3698b81c5cc67cc2907fea827c57ac5ce` and Shade MCP
commit `ac4c6ba14a8e8eb09b1e6f130ef0773cf0e750ff`. MCP request JSON is shown in
wire order. Each response is the JSON value decoded from the server's
`content[0].text` field.

### Authoring inputs

```js
import { Effect } from '../../../src/runtime/effect.js'

export default new Effect({
  name: "Test Pattern",
  namespace: "synth",
  func: "testPattern",
  tags: ["util"],

  description: "Test patterns for debugging and calibration",
  globals: {
    pattern: {
      type: "int",
      default: 0,
      uniform: "pattern",
      choices: { checkerboard: 0, colorBars: 1, gradient: 2, uvMap: 3, gridLines: 4, colorGrid: 5, dotGrid: 6 },
      ui: { label: "pattern", control: "dropdown" }
    },
    gridSize: {
      type: "int",
      default: 4,
      min: 1,
      max: 16,
      uniform: "gridSize",
      ui: {
        label: "grid size",
        control: "slider",
        enabledBy: { param: "pattern", in: [0, 4, 5, 6] }
      }
    }
  },
  passes: [
    {
      name: "main",
      program: "testPattern",
      inputs: {},
      outputs: {
        color: "outputTex"
      }
    }
  ]
})
```

<!-- WORKED:GLSL -->

`shaders/effects/synth/testPattern/glsl/testPattern.glsl`:

```glsl
#version 300 es
precision highp float;

uniform vec2 resolution;
uniform vec2 tileOffset;
uniform vec2 fullResolution;
uniform int gridSize;
uniform int pattern;

out vec4 fragColor;

// 3x5 pixel font for digits 0-9
// Each digit is encoded as 15 bits (3 columns x 5 rows, row-major)
const int GLYPH[10] = int[10](
    0x7B6F,  // 0: 111 101 101 101 111
    0x2492,  // 1: 010 010 010 010 010
    0x73E7,  // 2: 111 001 111 100 111
    0x72CF,  // 3: 111 001 011 001 111
    0x5BC9,  // 4: 101 101 111 001 001
    0x79CF,  // 5: 111 100 111 001 111
    0x79EF,  // 6: 111 100 111 101 111
    0x7249,  // 7: 111 001 001 001 001
    0x7BEF,  // 8: 111 101 111 101 111
    0x7BCF   // 9: 111 101 111 001 111
);

// Sample a glyph at local coordinates (0-2, 0-4)
bool sampleGlyph(int digit, int x, int y) {
    if (digit < 0 || digit > 9 || x < 0 || x > 2 || y < 0 || y > 4) return false;
    int bitIndex = y * 3 + (2 - x);  // row-major, top-left origin
    return ((GLYPH[digit] >> bitIndex) & 1) == 1;
}

// Render a number at a position within a cell
bool renderNumber(int number, vec2 cellUV) {
    // Determine how many digits we need
    int numDigits = 1;
    if (number >= 10) numDigits = 2;
    if (number >= 100) numDigits = 3;

    // Glyph dimensions in UV space (centered, cell-local)
    float glyphWidth = 0.15;
    float glyphHeight = 0.35;
    float spacing = 0.05;

    float totalWidth = float(numDigits) * glyphWidth + float(numDigits - 1) * spacing;
    float startX = 0.5 - totalWidth * 0.5;
    float startY = 0.5 - glyphHeight * 0.5;

    // Check if we're in the vertical range for glyphs
    if (cellUV.y < startY || cellUV.y >= startY + glyphHeight) return false;

    // Extract digits (right to left)
    int digits[3];
    int temp = number;
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        digits[i] = temp % 10;
        temp /= 10;
    }

    // Check each digit position (left to right)
    for (int d = 0; d < numDigits; d++) {
        float digitX = startX + float(d) * (glyphWidth + spacing);

        if (cellUV.x >= digitX && cellUV.x < digitX + glyphWidth) {
            // We're in this digit's horizontal range
            float localX = (cellUV.x - digitX) / glyphWidth;
            float localY = (cellUV.y - startY) / glyphHeight;

            // Map to 3x5 grid
            int gx = int(localX * 3.0);
            int gy = int(localY * 5.0);

            // Get the correct digit (numDigits-1-d because digits[] is reversed)
            int digit = digits[numDigits - 1 - d];

            return sampleGlyph(digit, gx, gy);
        }
    }

    return false;
}

// Pattern 0: Numbered checkerboard
vec4 checkerboard(vec2 uv) {
    int n = max(gridSize, 1);
    int cellX = int(uv.x * float(n)) % n;
    int cellY = int(uv.y * float(n)) % n;

    int cellNum = (n - 1 - cellY) * n + cellX;

    bool isWhiteCell = ((cellX + cellY) % 2) == 0;

    vec2 cellUV = fract(uv * float(n));

    bool isGlyph = renderNumber(cellNum, cellUV);

    float cellColor = isWhiteCell ? 1.0 : 0.0;
    float glyphColor = isWhiteCell ? 0.0 : 1.0;
    float finalColor = isGlyph ? glyphColor : cellColor;

    return vec4(vec3(finalColor), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 1: 8 vertical SMPTE-style color bars
vec4 colorBars(vec2 uv) {
    int bar = int(uv.x * 8.0);
    bar = clamp(bar, 0, 7);

    // white, yellow, cyan, green, magenta, red, blue, black
    vec3 colors[8] = vec3[8](
        vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
        vec3(1.0, 1.0, 0.0),
        vec3(0.0, 1.0, 1.0),
        vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0),
        vec3(1.0, 0.0, 1.0),
        vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0),
        vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    );

    return vec4(colors[bar], 1.0);
}

// Pattern 2: Horizontal black-to-white gradient ramp
vec4 gradient(vec2 uv) {
    return vec4(vec3(uv.x), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 3: UV map (R=u, G=v, B=0)
vec4 uvMap(vec2 uv) {
    return vec4(uv.x, uv.y, 0.0, 1.0);
}

// Pattern 4: Thin white grid lines on black
vec4 gridLines(vec2 uv) {
    int n = max(gridSize, 1);
    vec2 cellUV = fract(uv * float(n));
    vec2 edge = min(cellUV, 1.0 - cellUV);

    // Use direct calculation instead of fwidth() for tile-aware rendering.
    // This maintains the same line thickness in normal rendering while ensuring
    // continuity across tile boundaries during large-format print export.
    vec2 fw = vec2(1.0) / fullResolution * float(n);

    float line = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 2.0 * fw.x, edge.x) * smoothstep(0.0, 2.0 * fw.y, edge.y);
    return vec4(vec3(line), 1.0);
}

// HSV to RGB (hue only, full saturation & value)
vec3 hue2rgb(float h) {
    float r = abs(h * 6.0 - 3.0) - 1.0;
    float g = 2.0 - abs(h * 6.0 - 2.0);
    float b = 2.0 - abs(h * 6.0 - 4.0);
    return clamp(vec3(r, g, b), 0.0, 1.0);
}

// Pattern 5: Each cell gets a unique hue
vec4 colorGrid(vec2 uv) {
    int n = max(gridSize, 1);
    int cellX = int(uv.x * float(n)) % n;
    int cellY = int(uv.y * float(n)) % n;
    int cellIndex = cellY * n + cellX;
    float hue = fract(float(cellIndex) * 0.618033988749895);
    return vec4(hue2rgb(hue), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 6: Filled circle at each grid intersection
vec4 dotGrid(vec2 uv) {
    int n = max(gridSize, 1);
    vec2 scaled = uv * float(n);
    vec2 nearest = round(scaled);
    float dist = length(scaled - nearest);
    float dot = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.12, 0.15, dist);
    return vec4(vec3(dot), 1.0);
}

void main() {
    vec2 globalCoord = gl_FragCoord.xy + tileOffset;
    vec2 uv = globalCoord / fullResolution;

    if (pattern == 1) {
        fragColor = colorBars(uv);
    } else if (pattern == 2) {
        fragColor = gradient(uv);
    } else if (pattern == 3) {
        fragColor = uvMap(uv);
    } else if (pattern == 4) {
        fragColor = gridLines(uv);
    } else if (pattern == 5) {
        fragColor = colorGrid(uv);
    } else if (pattern == 6) {
        fragColor = dotGrid(uv);
    } else {
        fragColor = checkerboard(uv);
    }
}
```

<!-- WORKED:WGSL -->

`shaders/effects/synth/testPattern/wgsl/testPattern.wgsl`:

```wgsl
// WGSL version – WebGPU

struct Uniforms {
    resolution: vec2f,
    gridSize: i32,
    pattern: i32,
    tileOffset: vec2f,
    fullResolution: vec2f,
}

@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> uniforms: Uniforms;

// 3x5 pixel font for digits 0-9
// Each digit is encoded as 15 bits (3 columns x 5 rows, row-major)
const GLYPH = array<i32, 10>(
    0x7B6F,  // 0: 111 101 101 101 111
    0x2492,  // 1: 010 010 010 010 010
    0x73E7,  // 2: 111 001 111 100 111
    0x72CF,  // 3: 111 001 011 001 111
    0x5BC9,  // 4: 101 101 111 001 001
    0x79CF,  // 5: 111 100 111 001 111
    0x79EF,  // 6: 111 100 111 101 111
    0x7249,  // 7: 111 001 001 001 001
    0x7BEF,  // 8: 111 101 111 101 111
    0x7BCF   // 9: 111 101 111 001 111
);

// Sample a glyph at local coordinates (0-2, 0-4)
fn sampleGlyph(digit: i32, x: i32, y: i32) -> bool {
    if (digit < 0 || digit > 9 || x < 0 || x > 2 || y < 0 || y > 4) {
        return false;
    }
    let bitIndex = y * 3 + (2 - x);  // row-major, top-left origin
    return ((GLYPH[digit] >> u32(bitIndex)) & 1) == 1;
}

// Render a number at a position within a cell
fn renderNumber(number: i32, cellUV: vec2f) -> bool {
    // Determine how many digits we need
    var numDigits = 1;
    if (number >= 10) { numDigits = 2; }
    if (number >= 100) { numDigits = 3; }

    // Glyph dimensions in UV space (centered, scaled to fit nicely)
    let glyphWidth = 0.15;
    let glyphHeight = 0.35;
    let spacing = 0.05;

    let totalWidth = f32(numDigits) * glyphWidth + f32(numDigits - 1) * spacing;
    let startX = 0.5 - totalWidth * 0.5;
    let startY = 0.5 - glyphHeight * 0.5;

    // Check if we're in the vertical range for glyphs
    if (cellUV.y < startY || cellUV.y >= startY + glyphHeight) {
        return false;
    }

    // Extract digits (right to left)
    var digits = array<i32, 3>(0, 0, 0);
    var temp = number;
    for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        digits[i] = temp % 10;
        temp = temp / 10;
    }

    // Check each digit position (left to right)
    for (var d = 0; d < numDigits; d++) {
        let digitX = startX + f32(d) * (glyphWidth + spacing);

        if (cellUV.x >= digitX && cellUV.x < digitX + glyphWidth) {
            // We're in this digit's horizontal range
            let localX = (cellUV.x - digitX) / glyphWidth;
            let localY = (cellUV.y - startY) / glyphHeight;

            // Map to 3x5 grid
            let gx = i32(localX * 3.0);
            let gy = i32(localY * 5.0);

            // Get the correct digit (numDigits-1-d because digits[] is reversed)
            let digit = digits[numDigits - 1 - d];

            return sampleGlyph(digit, gx, gy);
        }
    }

    return false;
}

// Pattern 0: Numbered checkerboard
fn checkerboard(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    let n = max(uniforms.gridSize, 1);
    let cellX = i32(uv.x * f32(n)) % n;
    let cellY = i32(uv.y * f32(n)) % n;

    let cellNum = (n - 1 - cellY) * n + cellX;

    let isWhiteCell = ((cellX + cellY) % 2) == 0;

    let cellUV = fract(uv * f32(n));

    let isGlyph = renderNumber(cellNum, cellUV);

    let cellColor = select(0.0, 1.0, isWhiteCell);
    let glyphColor = select(1.0, 0.0, isWhiteCell);
    let finalColor = select(cellColor, glyphColor, isGlyph);

    return vec4f(vec3f(finalColor), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 1: 8 vertical SMPTE-style color bars
fn colorBars(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    var bar = i32(uv.x * 8.0);
    bar = clamp(bar, 0, 7);

    // white, yellow, cyan, green, magenta, red, blue, black
    let colors = array<vec3f, 8>(
        vec3f(1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
        vec3f(1.0, 1.0, 0.0),
        vec3f(0.0, 1.0, 1.0),
        vec3f(0.0, 1.0, 0.0),
        vec3f(1.0, 0.0, 1.0),
        vec3f(1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        vec3f(0.0, 0.0, 1.0),
        vec3f(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    );

    return vec4f(colors[bar], 1.0);
}

// Pattern 2: Horizontal black-to-white gradient ramp
fn gradientRamp(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    return vec4f(vec3f(uv.x), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 3: UV map (R=u, G=v, B=0)
fn uvMapPattern(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    return vec4f(uv.x, uv.y, 0.0, 1.0);
}

// Pattern 4: Thin white grid lines on black
fn gridLines(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    let n = max(uniforms.gridSize, 1);
    let cellUV = fract(uv * f32(n));
    let edge = min(cellUV, 1.0 - cellUV);
    // Non-tiling: original fwidth-based AA (byte-identical baseline).
    // Tiling: analytic AA width mirroring glsl/testPattern.glsl, which is
    // seam-stable across tiles where screen-space derivatives are not.
    let isTile = length(uniforms.tileOffset) > 0.0;
    // fwidthFine must be evaluated in uniform control flow (function scope),
    // so compute it unconditionally, then override only when tiling. The
    // analytic-width divide is skipped entirely on the non-tile path.
    var fw = fwidthFine(uv * f32(n));
    var edgeMul = 1.5;
    if (isTile) {
        let fr = select(uniforms.resolution, uniforms.fullResolution, uniforms.fullResolution.x > 0.0);
        fw = vec2f(1.0) / fr * f32(n);
        edgeMul = 2.0;
    }
    let line = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, edgeMul * fw.x, edge.x) * smoothstep(0.0, edgeMul * fw.y, edge.y);
    return vec4f(vec3f(line), 1.0);
}

// HSV to RGB (hue only, full saturation & value)
fn hue2rgb(h: f32) -> vec3f {
    let r = abs(h * 6.0 - 3.0) - 1.0;
    let g = 2.0 - abs(h * 6.0 - 2.0);
    let b = 2.0 - abs(h * 6.0 - 4.0);
    return clamp(vec3f(r, g, b), vec3f(0.0), vec3f(1.0));
}

// Pattern 5: Each cell gets a unique hue
fn colorGrid(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    let n = max(uniforms.gridSize, 1);
    let cellX = i32(uv.x * f32(n)) % n;
    let cellY = i32(uv.y * f32(n)) % n;
    let cellIndex = cellY * n + cellX;
    let hue = fract(f32(cellIndex) * 0.618033988749895);
    return vec4f(hue2rgb(hue), 1.0);
}

// Pattern 6: Filled circle at each grid intersection
fn dotGrid(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
    let n = max(uniforms.gridSize, 1);
    let scaled = uv * f32(n);
    let nearest = round(scaled);
    let dist = length(scaled - nearest);
    let d = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.12, 0.15, dist);
    return vec4f(vec3f(d), 1.0);
}

@fragment
fn main(@builtin(position) position: vec4f) -> @location(0) vec4f {
    // Tile-aware global UV (mirror glsl/testPattern.glsl). Non-tiling
    // (tileOffset=(0,0), fullResolution=resolution) is byte-identical.
    let fr = select(uniforms.resolution, uniforms.fullResolution, uniforms.fullResolution.x > 0.0);
    let uv = (position.xy + uniforms.tileOffset) / fr;

    if (uniforms.pattern == 1) {
        return colorBars(uv);
    } else if (uniforms.pattern == 2) {
        return gradientRamp(uv);
    } else if (uniforms.pattern == 3) {
        return uvMapPattern(uv);
    } else if (uniforms.pattern == 4) {
        return gridLines(uv);
    } else if (uniforms.pattern == 5) {
        return colorGrid(uv);
    } else if (uniforms.pattern == 6) {
        return dotGrid(uv);
    } else {
        return checkerboard(uv);
    }
}
```

The legal DSL invocation uses the generated enum identifier, writes the effect
chain to `o0`, and explicitly renders it:

```noisemaker
search synth
testPattern(pattern: checkerboard, gridSize: 4).write(o0)
render(o0)
```

`pattern` is a DSL `Identifier`, not the string literal `"checkerboard"`.
`gridSize` is a numeric expression. A direct `compileGraph()` call registers
the checked-in effect and expands this exact program to two expanded passes:

```json
[
  {"id":"node_0_pass_0","program":"node_0_testPattern","inputs":{},"outputs":{"color":"node_0_out"}},
  {"id":"node_1_write_blit","program":"blit","type":"render","inputs":{"src":"node_0_out"},"outputs":{"color":"global_o0"}}
]
```

The first is the one declared effect pass; the second is the terminal write
blit. A direct `compileGraph()` invocation against the pinned source reproduced
this exact pass array. No generator or repository contract test on current
`main` locks the worked example to the document; re-run the source-level check
under the freshness protocol when either pinned source changes.

Sources: `shaders/effects/synth/testPattern/definition.js` and its complete
GLSL/WGSL program files; `shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js` -
`registerEffectWithRuntime()` enum export; `shaders/src/runtime/expander.js` -
program expansion.

### Exact MCP validation-attempt transcript

<!-- WORKED:MCP-REQUESTS -->

Initialization used protocol `2025-06-18`; the following eight calls then ran
in a single server session. The response block is preserved literally. The two
`compileEffect` responses are evidence of GAP-024, not accepted validation:
WebGL2 returned three fallback-named passes and WebGPU returned one pass named
`main`, while the exact DSL above compiles to two. None of these eight
successful MCP results set `isError`.

Responses, in the same order:

```json
{"effect_id":"synth/testPattern","status":"ok","passes":[{"id":"pass_0","status":"ok"},{"id":"pass_1","status":"ok"},{"id":"pass_2","status":"ok"}],"message":"Compiled successfully","backend":"webgl2"}
{"effect_id":"synth/testPattern","status":"ok","passes":[{"id":"main","status":"ok"}],"message":"Compiled successfully","backend":"webgpu"}
{"effect_id":"synth/testPattern","status":"ok","backend":"WebGL2","frame":{"image_uri":null,"width":90,"height":90},"metrics":{"mean_rgb":[0.49851924975320827,0.49851924975320827,0.49851924975320827],"mean_alpha":1,"std_rgb":[0.49999780737389904,0.49999780737389904,0.49999780737389904],"luma_variance":0.2499978073787063,"unique_sampled_colors":2,"is_all_zero":false,"is_all_transparent":false,"is_essentially_blank":false,"is_monochrome":false}}

{"effect_id":"synth/testPattern","status":"skipped","isFilterEffect":false,"similarity":null,"details":"Not a filter effect"}
{"effect_id":"synth/testPattern","status":"ok","maxDiff":0,"meanDiff":0,"mismatchCount":0,"mismatchPercent":0,"resolution":[1024,1024],"glslSolid":false,"wgslSolid":false,"glslVariance":[16256,16256,16256],"wgslVariance":[16256,16256,16256],"yFlipDetected":false,"yFlipCleanFlip":false,"yFlipMismatchPercent":70.9,"yFlipMeanDiff":180.79,"yFlipRatio":1,"issues":[],"details":"Pixel parity OK (maxDiff=0, meanDiff=0.00)"}
{"effect_id":"synth/testPattern","status":"ok","backend":"webgl2","achieved_fps":54.6,"meets_target":true,"stats":{"frame_count":54,"avg_frame_time_ms":18.31,"jitter_ms":15.55,"min_frame_time_ms":5.3,"max_frame_time_ms":129.3}}
```

Falsifiable interpretation:

- Structure: pass because all issue arrays are empty and description exists.
- Compilation tool: **indeterminate**. WebGL2's three fallback-named passes and
  WebGPU's single `main` pass both conflict with the source-derived two-pass
  graph and are rejected under GAP-024. Their `backend` fields repeat configured
  session values and do not independently prove the page backend.
- Frame metrics: threshold pass because alpha `1 >= 0.01`, luma variance
  `0.2499978073787063 >= 0.0001`, sampled color count `2 > 1`, and no blank,
  transparent, or monochrome flag is set. Freshness is not proved by this verb
  because it shares GAP-024; the checkerboard metrics corroborate, but cannot
  machine-identify, the selected effect. There is no generic `>5` rendered-
  output requirement; that separate predicate belongs only to the filter
  modification tool.
- Uniform report: threshold pass because the only tested mutable uniform is
  `gridSize:pass`. `pattern` is a `choices` global and the tool intentionally
  excludes choices. Effect and backend freshness remain indeterminate under
  GAP-024.
- Passthrough report: expected skip because the definition has no `inputTex`
  input and therefore is not a filter. Effect and backend freshness remain
  indeterminate under GAP-024.
- Parity metric predicate: pass for the two captured buffers because
  `mismatchPercent = 0 < 1`, both solid flags are false, and no Y flip is
  detected. Effect freshness and requested-effect/backend identity are
  indeterminate:
  `waitReady()` can accept the previous noncompiling graph before asynchronous
  selection loads `synth/testPattern`, and `setBackend()` can time out silently.
  This call does not establish that either buffer came from the worked effect or
  its named backend. See GAP-024.
- Performance report: threshold pass because
  `achieved_fps = 54.6 >= target_fps = 30` and the returned `meets_target`
  agrees. The `backend` field is the configured session value; effect and
  actual-backend freshness remain indeterminate under GAP-024.

Thus the checked-in definition and shaders, structure report, and reproduced
two-pass source graph validate the authoring and expansion portions of this
worked effect. The recorded browser reports satisfy their numeric predicates
for whichever graph they captured, but none proves that graph was
`synth/testPattern`, and cross-backend reports do not prove each page backend.
End-to-end backend validation is therefore genuinely unfilled until Shade MCP
exposes and waits on effect, graph, and backend identity signals; this is
GAP-024, not a documentation value to invent.

The requested frame resolution was `[256,256]`, but the captured canvas was
`90x90`. Treat returned frame dimensions as authoritative and see GAP-021.

Sources: Shade MCP tool implementations and harness helpers cited in the tool
contract surface; the literal transcript above was produced by that server
against the two pinned source commits named at the start of this section.

## Surfaces x capabilities traceability matrix

<!-- TRACEABILITY-MATRIX -->

Every cell points to an executable contract or an explicitly identified gap.

| Surface | Introspect | Act | Validate | Diagnose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSL program | `Token`, `ParsedProgram`, `CompiledProgram`, registry keys, `CompiledGraph` | Complete EBNF plus call/read/write/render contracts | parse/unparse/compile and render metric predicates | `SyntaxError`, `Diagnostic`, `CompilationFailure`; GAP-001/002/023/027 |
| Effect definition | `Effect` fields, registry/manifest, `checkEffectStructure` | `EffectDefinition` typed grammar | validator and structure scan; browser backend identity is GAP-024 | exact validator messages, structural arrays, backend errors; GAP-003/007/024/026 |
| Parameters and globals | `effect.globals`, transformed `uniforms`, registry params | `GlobalSpec` typed grammar and enum/binding rules | compile reflection and numeric response deltas | transform errors, type/range/identity blind spots; GAP-010/011/024 |
| Passes and render graph | `Effect.passes`, `CompiledGraph.passes`, `CompiledGraph.textures`, `CompiledGraph.allocations` | `PassSpec` typed grammar and sampler/output binding rules | graph analysis and per-pass compile | unresolved inputs and backend compile/resource failures; GAP-005/006 |
| Textures and surface resources | texture specs plus runtime surface dimensions/formats | `TextureSpec` typed grammar and exact accepted policies | allocation existence, size/format inspection, render metrics | unsupported/missing surface failures and silent fields; GAP-004 |
| Compatibility and mutation | compiled AST, `listSteps`, `getCompatibleReplacements` | typed `replaceEffect` contract | candidate precheck; post-mutation browser identity is GAP-024 | compatibility and transform errors; GAP-008/022/024 |
| Rendered output | frame dimensions, `ImageMetrics`, sink stats, and `PackedFrame` | `RenderEffectFrameInput`, `Sink`, and `FrameExportQueue` contracts | exact metric predicates plus bounded queue/accounting rules | metric, capture, sink, and export failures; GAP-009/014/015/021/024/028 |
| Cross-backend parity | source-pair availability and parity report | GLSL ES 3.00/WGSL authoring contracts | buffer diff predicates; requested-effect/backend proof is GAP-024 | compile/readback/divergence/identity reports; GAP-012/016/024 |
| Shade MCP tool contracts | `tools/list`, effect scanners, all output types | Full signatures for all 18 verbs | verb-specific domain predicates | selector errors and tool-specific unions; GAP-013/017/018/019/020/024/029 |

External ports are deliberately outside this matrix. Their repositories define
separate candidate renderers, golden-image comparators, tolerance policies, and
failure reports. This document makes no cross-runtime validation claim for
those ports.

## Genuine engine instrumentation gaps

<!-- GAP-REGISTER -->

These are not documentation omissions. Each is behavior the inspected code does
not currently expose or enforce, so an agent cannot obtain the requested
contract without an engine/tool change.

| ID | Missing instrumentation | Source evidence | Agent consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| GAP-001 | No enforced `o0`-`o7` range | `shaders/src/lang/lexer.js` accepts digit-suffixed refs; `shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` - `createSurfaces()` preallocates only `o0`-`o7` | `o8` parses and fails later/indirectly instead of producing a range diagnostic |
| GAP-002 | Parser errors are thrown strings/`SyntaxError` without a stable diagnostic schema; `loc` is not documented as a public result | `shaders/src/lang/lexer.js`, `parser.js`, and `diagnostics.js` | retry code must parse human text and cannot reliably identify spans/codes |
| GAP-003 | `validateEffectDefinition()` validates only a subset of the consumed definition schema | `shaders/src/runtime/effect-validator.js` versus `effect.js` and `expander.js` | invalid globals/pass/texture fields can survive structure validation |
| GAP-004 | Mip and persistent-across-frames controls do not exist; definition-level 3D `filter` and unknown texture fields are discarded | `shaders/src/runtime/compiler.js` - `extractTextureSpecs()`; backend texture creation methods | an agent cannot author/query mip policy, persistence, or 3D nearest filtering, and typos can be ignored |
| GAP-005 | `name`, `conditions`, `viewport`, `clear`, `samplerTypes`, and `type` are not copied into expanded effect passes | `shaders/src/runtime/expander.js` - constructed pass object; `pipeline.js` - `shouldSkipPass()` | authoring these fields has no runtime effect through `definition.js` and emits no diagnostic |
| GAP-006 | Resource allocation/liveness output is analysis-only; renderers do not consume its physical allocation plan | `shaders/src/runtime/resources.js` - `analyzeLiveness()`/`allocateResources()`; `compiler.js` stores `graph.allocations` with no pipeline/backend consumer | an agent cannot query the actual runtime allocation/reuse plan promised by the analyzer |
| GAP-007 | Backend shader/compiler failures are not normalized to one structured diagnostic union | `shaders/src/runtime/backends/webgl2.js` and `webgpu.js`; Shade browser tool wrappers | backend retry logic must parse browser/compiler strings |
| GAP-008 | Replace compatibility checks only target existence plus starter/nonstarter chain position and is not an MCP preflight verb | `shaders/src/lang/transform.js` - `getCompatibleReplacements()` and `replaceEffect()` | arguments, sampler topology, shader availability, types, ranges, passes, outputs, and backend support are not predicted before mutation |
| GAP-009 | No temporal no-animation metric or universal low-variety metric is returned by `renderEffectFrame` | Shade `src/tools/browser/render.ts`; filter-only temporal/color logic is in `passthrough.ts` | no-animation requires an external two-frame comparison; low variety needs effect exemptions |
| GAP-010 | Uniform responsiveness returns overall `ok` when any tested uniform passes | Shade `src/tools/browser/uniforms.ts` - `testUniformResponsiveness()` | caller must inspect every `tested_uniforms` entry; outer status is unsafe |
| GAP-011 | Uniform responsiveness omits measured luma/channel deltas | Shade `src/tools/browser/uniforms.ts` - returned object | caller cannot audit the `>0.002` threshold from the report alone |
| GAP-012 | Upstream `renderEffectFrame` does not implement WebGPU pixel readback | Shade `src/tools/browser/render.ts` reads only `pipeline.backend.gl` | authoring can compile on WebGPU but single-backend frame metrics are unavailable there |
| GAP-013 | Noisemaker MCP config tracks an unpinned GitHub package reference | `.mcp.json` | tool schemas/thresholds can drift independently of this document snapshot |
| GAP-014 | A positive explicit `time` with warmup frames can pause animation before the awaited frame count and hang the tool | Shade `src/tools/browser/render.ts` pauses before its frame-count warmup promise; observed run reproduced the hang | a valid-looking render request can fail to terminate |
| GAP-015 | Similar metrics are computed by separate helpers with different sample grids/blank heuristics | Shade `src/tools/browser/render.ts`, `dsl.ts`, and `parity.ts`; Noisemaker `vendor/shade-mcp/harness/pixel-reader.js` | metric names cannot be assumed numerically interchangeable across verbs |
| GAP-016 | No preflight reports whether an effect is authorable/renderable on each backend before compilation | `shaders/src/renderer/canvas.js` - shader discovery; backend `compileProgram()` methods | impossible parity cases are found only by source/compile failure |
| GAP-017 | Shade's definition parser is regex-based and lossy | Shade `src/formats/definition-js.ts` - `parseDefinitionJs()` | list/analysis tools cannot expose the complete Noisemaker definition schema |
| GAP-018 | MCP selector inputs described as globs are compared literally | Shade `src/tools/resolve-effects.ts` - `resolveEffectIds()` | wildcard-looking selectors silently do not expand |
| GAP-019 | `testNoPassthrough` varies time/color rather than injecting and comparing an input texture | Shade `src/tools/browser/passthrough.ts` - `testNoPassthrough()` | its name overstates what is measured; true input passthrough is not tested |
| GAP-020 | MCP tools have a shared whole-call `isError` marker but no shared domain error envelope | Shade `src/tools/tool-result.ts` marks top-level object failures; all 18 handlers use it for ordinary returns, while batch arrays retain per-entry incompatible unions | partial batch failures and verb-specific payload success/failure still cannot be handled uniformly, and callers must not assume every error text is JSON |
| GAP-021 | `renderEffectFrame` requested resolution can differ from returned canvas dimensions without a warning | Shade `src/tools/browser/render.ts` sets viewport but reads canvas dimensions; exact transcript requested `256x256` and returned `90x90` | thresholds run on an unexpected sample size unless the caller checks `frame.width/height` |
| GAP-022 | RESOLVED. `StepInfo` now carries `kind` (`'effect'`/`'builtin'`); builtins report `canReplaceWith*` false, and `replaceEffect()`/`getCompatibleReplacements()` reject a builtin `stepIndex` | `shaders/src/lang/transform.js` - `isBuiltinOp()`, `listSteps()`, `replaceEffect()`, `getCompatibleReplacements()`; covered by `shaders/tests/test_transform.js` | none |
| GAP-023 | `test_compiler_phase2.js` catches assertion failures without setting a nonzero process exit code | `shaders/tests/test_compiler_phase2.js` - `test()` catch only writes `console.error` | automation can report process success while the suite prints `FAIL`; callers must scan output until the harness is fixed |
| GAP-024 | Browser MCP readiness and backend switching are not bound to requested effect, compiled graph, and actual backend identity | Shade `src/tools/browser/compile.ts`, `render.ts`, `benchmark.ts`, `uniforms.ts`, `passthrough.ts`, and `dsl.ts` poll status text; `describe.ts` delegates to `renderEffectFrame`; `src/tools/browser/parity.ts` waits only for a noncompiling nonempty graph; `src/harness/browser-session.ts` dispatches selection without awaiting the Noisemaker asynchronous load and `setBackend()` silently exits after its poll timeout | any browser `ok` result, including parity, can describe a previously ready graph or unintended backend; configured backend labels do not prove page state, and no current result field makes those identity mismatches uniformly diagnosable |
| GAP-026 | `onInit`, `onUpdate`, and `onDestroy` are copied into `Effect` wrappers but are not invoked by the production renderer | `shaders/src/runtime/effect.js` defines the wrappers; only `shaders/tests/harness_effect.js` calls them; `shaders/src/runtime/pipeline.js` calls `asyncInit` only | an authored config callback can look valid but never run in production; use only `asyncInit` as a production lifecycle hook until callers exist |
| GAP-027 | Subchain arguments have no enforced key set, separator rule, duplicate-key diagnostic, or discarded-key report | `shaders/src/lang/parser.js` - `parseSubchainCall()` accepts arbitrary identifier/string pairs, makes commas optional, overwrites duplicates in `kwargs`, and projects only `name`/`id` into the AST | a typo or unknown subchain key can parse successfully and disappear; retry logic receives no machine-readable failure |
| GAP-028 | Frame export has no terminal result or cancellation counter for accepted frames discarded by reconfigure or close | `shaders/src/runtime/frame-export.js` - `configure()`, `close()`, `_destroySlots()`, `_release()` | accepted work can lose its callback without incrementing `completed`, `failed`, or `dropped`, so a host cannot reconcile or selectively retry canceled frames |
| GAP-029 | Effect-index invalidation does not supersede an in-flight rebuild | Shade `src/knowledge/shared-instances.ts` leaves `building` intact in `invalidateSharedEffectIndex()` and shares it with the next reader | a list/search immediately after a library change or `generateManifest` can retain a pre-change index for the next five-second TTL; retry after that TTL when freshness matters |

The matrix has 9 surfaces x 4 capabilities = 36 filled cells. Cells that rely
on behavior absent from code link to the 28 gaps above rather than substituting
an invented contract.
